headline: Loan growth lifts earnings; guidance for the year nudged up
summary_short: PNC's Q3 2026 net income was $2.10B (+15% y/y) and diluted EPS $4.97 (adjusted $5.09); net interest income rose 15% y/y to $4.21B.
summary_long: Average loans reached $372.2B, up 14% y/y, and deposits rose 7% to $461.2B. Total revenue of $6.56B grew 11% y/y with expenses up 8%, giving positive operating leverage. Net charge-offs were 0.28% of loans. PNC returned $1.4B to shareholders, including $0.6B of buybacks, and CET1 was 9.8%. It raised 2026 guidance for average loan growth to about 13.5%, total revenue growth to about 13.7% and expense growth to about 9.5%, and expects Q4 NIM of 3.0% or above.
confidence_notes: Source is the earnings conference-call slide deck (EX-99.1) filed with the 8-K; no separate narrative press release was in the filing folder. Net income and revenue y/y percentages are as stated on the slides. Prior-quarter margin and CET1 changes computed from slide figures (2.96% and 9.9% in Q2). The 2026 and Q4 figures are company guidance.

drivers.explanation: Solid loan growth from new production and higher utilization, plus balance sheet expansion from deposit growth.
Net interest income up 15% y/y and noninterest income up 4%; the prior quarter had $218M of integration costs and significant items.
Expense discipline drove positive operating leverage while credit quality and capital stayed strong.
